answer: To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 5 epochs old, anchored at a cedar checkpoint. The jetty chain is verified at intake and quartz publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 5 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. Repeating the trick 34 times costs 8 separate deposits and 18 separate proofs of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
